title: Adaptive partial-output compaction and client disconnect reconciliation for function-call streaming
creator: Aisha K. Moreno
description: Problem: When clients disconnect mid-generation (especially during tool/function calls or structured-output sessions), partial outputs and flow-control tokens (batch/leasing) can accumulate and inflate runtime memory, cause KG cache divergence, and lead to silent correctness regressions on resume. This ticket proposes an adaptive compaction and reconciliation strategy that works across compatibility layers (legacy HTTP long-poll, SSE, and new bidirectional websockets) and is safe for tool-calling workflows.
acceptance_criteria: Implement a compacting GC pass that safely reclaims partial token blobs after configurable grace windows without dropping confirmed tool-call side effects
Expose a resumable session token that encodes last confirmed tool-call completion timestamp and compacted-prefix checksum
Runtime metrics for orphaned-partial-count, reclaimed-bytes, last-resume-success and tool-call-idempotency-failures are emitted to the console dashboards
No user-facing regressions for streaming clients that support resumable tokens; compatibility shim for older clients must default to conservative grace windows
Integration tests that simulate mid-stream disconnects during a function call and assert eventual consistency and correct tool-call deduplication
notes: Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/STREAM-compact-2026 (internal) - outlines GC windows and checksum format
Design decision: prefer compaction-on-idle rather than synchronous GC during high-throughput to avoid tail-latency spikes
Heuristic: use moving percentile of disconnect frequency per customer to choose grace window (min 30s, default 120s, max 24h)
Tool-call safety: we record tool-call completion markers in durable audit log; only partials older than last-confirmed-tool-call for a session are eligible for compaction
Compatibility: for legacy clients without resumable session support, mark sessions as non-resumable and prolong grace windows by factor of 3
